Reheated leftovers should reach a core temperature of 74 degrees C before serving.

Filler paragraph so this fixture page clears the fetch layer's near-empty-page floor: reheating food evenly matters because cold spots in the middle of a dish can let bacteria survive even when the outside looks piping hot, which is why a probe thermometer reading from the thickest part of the food is the only reliable check, not how long the dish has spent in the oven or how hot the plate feels to the touch when it comes out.
